stem: Which trigger is most typical for asthma exacerbations in a school-aged child?
explanation: Respiratory viral infection is the most typical trigger for asthma exacerbations in children.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Respiratory viral infections commonly precipitate asthma symptoms in school-aged children, making them the most typical trigger among the options.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because respiratory viral infection is the most common and typical trigger for asthma exacerbations in children.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an inhaled foreign body can cause acute respiratory symptoms but is not the usual trigger for asthma exacerbations.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because anaphylaxis may cause wheeze and respiratory compromise, but it is not the typical trigger for asthma exacerbations.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because tonsillar hypertrophy causes upper-airway obstruction rather than typical asthma exacerbations.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ACE inhibitor use can cause cough, but it is not a typical trigger for asthma exacerbations in children.
